items.html: Now we will explain the second state in the ten Sefirot, being the light of straightness, which is similar to three lines in the form of the upper Adam. Through that line, which expands from above downward, and from which the circles expand, that line also expands, in straightness from above downward, from the top of the roof 1 of the top circle, to below the bottom of the end of all the circles from above downward. It consists of ten Sefirot, like the image of a straight Adam 2, upright 3, consisting of 248 organs 4 depicted as three lines: right, left, and middle. He consists of ten Sefirot overall, and each and every Sefira is divided into ten Sefirot indefinitely.

There are five kinds of light in the lower Adam 5: Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama, Haya, Yechida 6. They are five levels 7, one above the other, and this is the meaning of the five repetitions of the verse, “Bless the Lord, O my soul, etc.” as mentioned in Masechet Berachot (p 10, 70a), which correspond to the five phases of the soul.

Each of the ten Sefirot of the circles has all the above phases, namely lights and vessels 8. The light is divided 9 into inner light and surrounding light, and the vessel is divided 10into externality and internality. The ten Sefirot of straightness in the image of Adam have all those phases, too.

The difference between the circles and the straightness relates to the fact that the ten Sefirot of circles 20 are regarded as the light of Nefesh. There are inner light and Surrounding Light in them, internal and external. They consist of ten Sefirot of vessels, and in each vessel, there are internality and externality. There are also ten Sefirot of lights, where in each light there are inner light and surrounding light.
However, the ten Sefirot of straightness are regarded as the light called light of Ruach 30, which is a higher degree than the degree of Nefesh. They, too, consist of inner light and surrounding light, and have ten Sefirot of vessels, and in each of them there are internality and externality. Obviously, the Nefesh was emanated first, and the Ruach next.

Even when the ten Sefirot are regarded as circles 40 one within the other, they already have all the states of reception of the abundance that exist in the ten Sefirot in the line of straightness 50. It is so because the circle of Keter, called Arich Anpin after the correction 60, has one hole and window 70 on the right side of the circle 80. From there, the light of Arich descends to the circle of Abba and shines to it 90.
There is another window, on the left side of the circle of Arich, and the light exits until the left side of the circle of Abba, which is within it, punctures it and makes a window in it 100. The light is extended from there to the circle of Ima inside the circle of Abba, and shines in it. It turns out that when the light passes in the left of the circle of Abba, it is not for Abba himself; it passes there only as a passageway 200, but the illumination is primarily for Ima.
It follows that Arich Anpin shines for Abba and Ima together, just as it is in their straightness. Even though they are one circle within the other, they still have straight lines, 300 right, left and middle, in the windows in them. The light is extended from there in ten Sefirot of circles, through completely straight lines, in all the details in the ten Sefirot of the straight line of Ruach.

That AK 400 is extended from one end to the other 1, from the top end to the bottom end throughout the above space of Atzilut. All the worlds are contained in that Adam, but we have no permission whatsoever to speak and to engage in the internality and self of that Adam 2.

In the beginning, the ten Sefirot came out through a circle 3, one within the other. Afterwards, within the circles, they were extended in straightness as an image of one Adam, throughout the length of all the above-mentioned circles 4. Still, we do not engage in the circles whatsoever 5, but only in the straightness.
